observations: Photo 0 shows a silver Casio keyboard with 61 keys, wrapped in plastic, placed on artificial grass. The model 'CTK-900' is visible on the left side near the keys.

Photo 1 shows a close-up of the right side of the keyboard, with the Casio logo, power switch, volume knob, and speaker grille. The model number 'CTK-900' is not visible here, but the 'CTK-800' label is not present.
Photo 2 shows a close-up of the left side of the keyboard, clearly displaying the model 'CTK-800' printed on the panel. The 'Touch Response' label and USB port are also visible.
The keyboard appears to be new or unused, still in plastic wrapping. There are no visible signs of damage or wear.
The seller claims it is a 'CTK-900', but photo 2 clearly shows 'CTK-800'.

claims.evidence: Photo 2 clearly shows the model as 'CTK-800', not 'CTK-900'.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be functional despite appearing new.
risks.proof: A video clip showing the keyboard powered on, keys responding, and sound output.

risks.risk: The keyboard may have internal damage or defects not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A close-up video of the internal components or a test of all keys and functions.
risks.if_unproven: priced at lower end of market range for CTK-800

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powered on and playing a note to confirm functionality.
Close-up of the power switch and indicator light to confirm it turns on.
Check for any missing or damaged keys or buttons.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Casio CTK-800 keyboard from photo 2. The seller's claim of 'CTK-900' is contradicted by the visible model label. The keyboard appears new and wrapped, but functionality is unverified. It can be priced at its worst case (not working) until proven functional.
